title: Voice AI Sees Major Acquisition: ElevenLabs Announces Acquisition of Renowned Japanese Voice AI Company Kotoba

content_html:
The global voice AI industry has seen a high-profile consolidation. Well-known voice AI company ElevenLabs recently officially announced that it has successfully acquired Kotoba, a leading Japanese voice AI lab. Through this powerful partnership, the two sides will work together to accelerate the deep adoption and widespread use of AI agents and voice interaction interfaces in the world’s fourth-largest economy.

Breaking Down Language and Cultural Barriers: Building Voice AI That Adapts to Deep Local Context

Human language communication is not just a combination of literal words; it also carries strong regional flavor, complex dialect accents, and unwritten social and cultural norms. By contrast, languages such as Japanese tend to be more nuanced and context-dependent in expression—for example, sentences often omit subjects and objects, word choice changes in real time depending on whom one is speaking to, people habitually maintain social politeness through frequent apologies, pauses are used to indicate thinking, and there is even a unique culture of “reading the air” (kūki o yomu), meaning the need to understand what is implied rather than said.

Recognizing this complexity of cross-cultural interaction, ElevenLabs has made it a core mission to “make AI natural and intuitive across different cultures and contexts.” With its deep voice technology research and profound understanding of the Japanese local market, Kotoba became the natural partner to achieve this goal.

Kotoba was founded in Tokyo in 2023 by AI researchers Noriyuki Kojima and Jungo Kasai. Its founding mission was to develop voice AI for a multilingual world, firmly believing that “voice should not stop at the boundaries of language.”
